mentions.name: Opair
mentions.description: A coding harness for AI agents that eschews autonomy: tools grant access to specific executables with dangerous arguments blockable instead of shell access, separate driver and navigator modes enable or block writable tool access, and role-based model configuration controls model options depending on whether the agent is planning, reviewing, or driving. Currently WIP with no installation process yet, but used by its author as a daily driver in preference to Claude Code.

mentions.name: opair
mentions.description: Opair is a coding harness that eschews autonomy and instead works like a pair programming partner, with distinct "driver" and "navigator" modes. It is early-stage (a few weekends of work so far) and already used to develop itself.
mentions.problem: The author got frustrated that nobody else was building the coding harness they actually wanted to use.
mentions.source_excerpt: It's a coding harness that eschews autonomy and instead works like a pair programming partner, with distinct "driver" and "navigator" modes. I've only spent 3 weekends on it so far, so it's a long way from finished. But I am at least using opair to work on opair now, which is nice.
